A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MetaOthello study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original transformer-training results, probe measurements, representational alignment, and causal steering experiments in Table 1, Figures 2–6, and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds component-level circuit localization, ablation, and steering results in Section 5.4.2 and Figure 6.

M1.justification: Section 5.4.2 extends the intervention procedure from residual-stream game-identity steering to learned component-specific directions applied jointly to the identified MLP–attention-head–MLP circuit. The game framework, transformer architecture, training, and original probing/alignment procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use Classic, NoMidFlip, DelFlank, and Iago, including the same pure/mixed training coverage and ambiguous-prefix scenarios. The added circuit experiments investigate existing game and prefix conditions rather than introducing new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: The new circuit experiment compares full-circuit steering with routing-head-only steering and a runner-up layer-5 head using its own learned direction; Figure 6b labels the latter H0 control. Existing random-probe, one-hot-input, null-intervention, and matched/cross-probe comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Section 5.4.2 adds a substantial component-level evaluation protocol: separate direction-learning and held-out steering sets, readouts before attention/after attention/after MLP, and last-token component ablations. New measurements include signed game-ID margins, unique-move branch preference, and wrong-game probability mass. Existing model-training and benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 localized effective NoMidFlip steering to layer 5. v2 adds component and individual-head ablations, tile-conflict projection analysis, steering-strength sensitivity, and controlled circuit steering. These tests investigate which components construct and route game identity and whether the localized circuit causally controls branch selection.

E5.justification: The added circuit analysis reports 1,000 bootstrap resamples for head-ranking stability and a Mann–Whitney test with a rank-biserial effect size. Existing confidence-interval reporting and Appendix A.4's fixed seed 42 and single model-training run are retained; the bootstrap does not establish additional training runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial circuit results, including Classic unique-move probability share changing from 0.48 to 0.68 or 0.01 under directional steering, and wrong-game mass increasing from 0.0001 to 0.0115 under ablation. All 12 Table 1 means and intervals and existing plotted results are retained. DelFlank accuracies of 77.4% and 75.8% are now correctly attributed in prose to layers 2 and 3, matching both versions' plots.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the stated move-set cardinality from '64 (or 65, including pass)' to 65 for the explicitly defined set containing all board positions and pass. The game-transition mathematics, Bayesian mixture derivation, and normalized-KL alpha score otherwise remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion elevate a specifically identified, causally steerable routing circuit to a central contribution. v1 leaves the coexistence of shared representations and game-specific predictions unresolved; v2 claims to resolve it through localized conflict processing and emphasizes distinct mid-layer reweighting and early-selection regimes.

C2.justification: v2 introduces a mechanism in which the layer-4 MLP constructs conflict features and layer-5 components route them, and develops the contrast between NoMidFlip reweighting and DelFlank selection. Appendix C.1 adds an explanation of final-layer Iago intervention behavior. It also removes v1's explicit warning that rotational isomorphism alone cannot distinguish one shared representation from multiple similarly structured representations.

D1.justification: v2 specifies component intervention sites, last-token-output zeroing, and activation readout locations for the new circuit analysis. Appendix A's architecture, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, probe-training details, and code/model/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Millière and Buckner, Mitchell, Schönemann, and Sikarwar et al., and removes Li et al. (2025) and Richens et al. It clarifies representational versus forward-dynamics meanings of world models while retaining the central positioning against vocabulary-only mOthello. Park et al.'s publication update represents the same work.

P1.justification: The abstract, related-work opening, ambiguity/OOD discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting and condensation. Former Section 5.5 becomes 5.4.1 alongside the new mechanism subsection; v2 also adds Appendix C.1 and acknowledgments and edits publication information and terminology.

P2.justification: v2 adds a two-panel Figure 6 showing circuit readouts and controlled steering. Existing plots are retained, with some relocation/rescaling and subsequent renumbering; the DelFlank caption corrects layers 1–2 to 2–3. Table 1 is repositioned and its game-name capitalization standardized.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly leaves its central mechanistic puzzle unresolved after layer-level steering. v2's component ablations, matched head control, and held-out circuit steering provide substantially stronger causal evidence for a specific conflict-routing mechanism, materially strengthening the paper's explanatory contribution. Removing the useful Iago-isomorphism caveat weakens qualification, but the new controlled evidence provides a clear net improvement.
